title: Probabilistic demand-smoothing autoscaler for dedicated fleets
creator: Arjun Patel
description:
Background: Dedicated fleets must provide predictable throughput guarantees while avoiding costly overprovisioning. Current step-based autoscalers react to short-term spikes or long averages and either oscillate or overcommit for bursty inference traffic. This ticket proposes a probabilistic demand-smoothing autoscaler that reasons about demand uncertainty and enforces conservative safety envelopes to balance latency SLOs and unit cost.

Goals: 1) Maintain latency SLOs (p95 latency per-tenant) under typical and bursty traffic patterns. 2) Reduce excess capacity spend vs simple reactive autoscalers. 3) Provide clear, auditable safety limits and runtime controls (max scale step, min floor, burst allowance). 4) Make behavior explainable to platform and tenant owners (telemetry + deterministic config).

Key metrics and targets: - Primary target metric: predicted sustained tokens/sec demand per-tenant (tokens/s or request RPS adjusted by avg tokens). - Secondary metric: p95 response latency and p99 tail latency for short-lived requests. - Safety thresholds: never scale below min_replicas; cap scale-out to max_scale_step per minute; permit short bursts up to burst_multiplier * capacity for max_burst_duration seconds before emergency scale.

Algorithm overview: - Demand estimator: ingest recent request stream and compute a short-term stochastic demand forecast using an exponentially-weighted Poisson smoothing model. The estimator outputs a demand distribution (forecast quantiles) rather than a single point estimate. - Quantile-based target: compute required capacity at a configurable quantile (default q=0.95) of the demand distribution, converting demand -> required replicas via per-replica throughput profile. - Smoothing window: combine multi-window estimates (fast window e.g., 15s, medium 2m, slow 10m) with weighted blending to avoid reacting to single outlier events. - Scale decision rules: scale-out if q95 forecast > current_capacity * headroom_target; scale-in only when q50 forecast < current_capacity * shrink_threshold AND sustained for cooldown period. - Slew and step control: impose a capped delta per control interval (max_scale_step) and a slew-rate limiter to prevent >X replicas/minute. - Emergency path: if observed latency breaches emergency_latency_threshold and predicted demand remains high, bypass slow windows and allow emergency_scale up to emergency_max_step subject to cost guardrail. - Cost guardrail: if estimated incremental cost of scale-out would exceed budgetized burst budget in the billing window, prefer lightweight mitigations (shorter inference tokens limit, returning 429 for low-priority tenants) and record decision for audit.

Config knobs (initial defaults): - smoothing_alpha_fast: "0.6" - smoothing_alpha_med: "0.2" - smoothing_alpha_slow: "0.05" - forecast_quantile: "0.95" - lookback_fast_s: "15" - lookback_med_s: "120" - lookback_slow_s: "600" - max_scale_step: "4" (replicas) - slew_rate_per_min: "6" (replicas/min) - min_replicas: "2" - max_replicas: "200" - cooldown_s: "180" - burst_multiplier: "2.5" - max_burst_duration_s: "30" - emergency_latency_threshold_ms: "1200" - emergency_max_step: "12" - cost_burst_budget_usd: "500"

Safety limits and rationale: - Min/max replica constraints avoid oscillation and runaway scale. - Quantile-based capacity gives explicit confidence level for meeting demand; teams can tune quantile per workload criticality. - Multi-window smoothing prevents edge-triggering on single noisy spikes while still preserving responsiveness to sustained increases. - Slew/rate caps and cooldowns protect upstream provisioning and downstream infra (e.g., cluster boot storms). - Emergency path is explicit and auditable: it requires both observed latency breach AND forecasted elevated demand.

Telemetry, observability and rollouts: - Expose the following per-tenant time series: forecast quantiles (p50/p75/p95), chosen target_replicas, actual_replicas, scale_actions (timestamped), latency p50/p95/p99, and cost estimate for recent window. - Dashboards: autoscale decisions timeline, false-positive/false-negative classification for scaling events, and cost delta vs baseline reactive policy. - Tracing: annotate scale decisions with inputs and rule matched for deterministic debugging. - Canary rollout: start with internal test tenants for 48h, then opt-in beta for 5 customers, then gradual account-wide ramp with ability to pin tenants to legacy autoscaler.

Acceptance criteria: 1) Implementation produces stable capacity decisions under synthetic burst tests (Poisson bursts and diurnal patterns) without violating p95 latency target for internal test tenants. 2) CPU/GPU utilization variance decreases by >=10% vs baseline over 1h test while cost per token does not increase by more than 5%. 3) Scale actions are annotated and visible in console; prospective customers can select forecast_quantile and burst_multiplier. 4) Safety guards prevent >2x provisioning above baseline except during explicit emergency path.

Rollout plan and tasks: - Spike: build demand estimator library and unit tests (owner: Maya Chen) - Integration: wire estimator into policy engine, implement decision rules and safeties (owner: Backend Runtime) - Telemetry: add metrics and dashboard templates (owner: Observability team) - E2E tests: synthetic workload harness and chaos tests for scale coordination (owner: SRE) - Documentation: console controls and runbook for emergency path (owner: PM)

Open questions: - How should cross-tenant fairness be enforced when fleet capacity is constrained? (tenant priority queue vs proportional degradation) - Should we expose burst allowance per-tenant or per-pool? - Precise cost accounting for short bursts (cloud billing granularity) requires coordination with finance.
